evidence.quote: The mechanical properties of Ti-Nb-O alloys were determined by uniaxial tensile test and micro-hardness test at room temperature.

The rapid increase of micro-hardness of Ti-32Nb-0.2O alloy compared to Ti–32Nb alloy is due to the presence of ω phase.
The passive current densities are nearly stable when the potential increases from 0.55 V to 1.61 V, indicating a passive region.
The corrosion current density of Ti-Nb-O alloys except for Ti–32Nb and Ti–38Nb alloys is lower than those of Ti-6Al-4 V alloy (0.30 μA/cm2) and 316 L stainless steel (0.82 μA/cm2)

The values of micro-hardness increase monotonously with the increase of oxygen concentration at constant Nb content, resulting from the solid solution strengthening of interstitial oxygen.
The rapid increase of micro-hardness of Ti-32Nb-0.2O alloy compared to Ti–32Nb alloy is due to the presence of ω phase.
The Ti–32Nb and Ti-32Nb-0.2O alloys show an obvious double yielding behavior, which is the typical stress-induced martensitic transformation of metastable β-type Ti alloys.
However, the deformation mode of the Ti-38Nb-0.5O alloy is dominated by dislocation slipping, with a distinct yield drop limited work hardening.
